text:
When a selected trope name is selected, such as V'ahavta,  the screen disiplays a number of lines with the tropes used for the words that will be chanted for that line.  The format is to use the trope name text,  that corresponds to the names in the trope table on the main display, separated by a plus sign.  The lines are not significant and the number of words per line is set for display purposes,  but lines should not continue past a Sof Pasuk or one of the Aliyah ending tropes.  If the title box containing the name of the portion at the top of the display is clicked,   another series of lines will appear with the Hebrew lyric text of that portion that is marked with the cantiallation symbols. Clicking the box again, will hide the display of Hebrew lyrics. If the chosen portion does not have this information avaiailable,  these lines will not appear. 

This screen is intended to provide audio playback of trope melodies.  Clicking any of the  lines with the trope name sequence will trigger a playback of generic trope melodies for each of the listed tropes in the line.  At the top of the display are two check boxes,  one for sequential playbak and one for smooth playback.  When the former is set,  each of the trope names will be highlighted and the corresponding melody will be played and the process repeats for all names in the line until the line is completed. The playback melody is a generic sound with no attempt to vocalize the pronunciation,  but rather the sound of someone humming or vocalizing a series of 'aahs' for each note in the trope melody. In smooth mode,  no highlighting occurs and the tropes are played in sequence. If a Hebrew lyrics line is clcked,  the audio playback will be a vocalization and pronunciation of the actual Hebrew words in that line. If a mouse is used and the cursor hovers over a Hebrew word in the lyrics that word is highlighted and a tool tip winow opens with the word's English transliteration.  If using a touch device,  the hover action is triggered by touching and holding one's finger on the target.  The tool tip should disappear when the target is no longer selected by either mechanism.

The trope name generic playback results from audio files geneated by the 'Musescore' program where the melody was defined on a music staff by specifying the note pattern for that trope.  There was no attempt to provide mulitple note patterns for variations in pitch required by the lyrics,  thus a standard note patterns is played for all tropes with the exception of Munach which depends upon the subsequent note in the sequence.  The lyrics playback was generated by using 'TropeTrainer.Com' which is designed to generate the melodies and pronuncaition of actual text and thus variations in pitch and time durations to accomodate additional syllables  in words not represented in the generic playback will be heard.  The sounds of the two playback options differ somewhat in that the generic trope names are of a higher pitch than the voice used for the lyrics and the generic 'aah' sounds represent a sound produced by a choir rater than an individual. Note that the generic note sequence used for the trope name playback can be viewed from the main trope table by clicking the trope name in the table to open the Trope Info display which includes the musical note notation for each of the tropes using a standard five line music staff.
